welcome_page.title: Public transport – Safety and comfort
welcome_page.description:
Stops, crossings and situations on the way when you use public transport.

Taking part is voluntary. To continue, answer each question shown. Where offered, you can choose “Prefer not to say”. Your answers are not linked to your name, and no public authority receives them.

Learn more about SmartUrbanity

Only the SmartUrbanity research team reads your answers. We keep them for research for 36 months; then we delete them or make them anonymous.

  • Public transport – Road safety
  • Public transport – Personal security
  • Public transport – Comfort

final_page.title: Thank you!
final_page.description: Your submission has been recorded. Thank you for taking the time to complete the questionnaire.

questionnaire.title: Public transport – Safety and comfort

questions.text: What problems do you meet at stops or when getting on and off?

options.text: Hard to get on or off the vehicle
Broken or poorly kept stops (e.g. broken lifts, damaged shelters)
Stop or vehicle cannot be used with a wheelchair, walker or stroller
Vehicles too crowded to get on with a stroller or wheelchair
The ramp does not work or is not deployed when needed
Vehicles so full that I have to wait for the next one
No sidewalk or walkway to reach the stop
No real-time arrival information, on screen or announced

questions.text: When you cross the road to reach or leave a stop, how safe do you feel?
questions.help: Think of traffic lights, zebra crossings, footbridges or underpasses near the stops you use.

questions.text: Because of the crossings near the stops, do you…?
When you use public transport, which of these situations make you feel unsafe? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Unsafe behaviour from drivers, riders or pedestrians
Lack of safe or adequate stops, crossings or lighting

questions.text: During the day, do you ever feel unsafe from crime or harassment when you use public transport? (Harassment includes unwanted comments, following, touching, or intimidating behaviour directed at you.)
In the evening or after dark, do you ever feel unsafe from crime or harassment when you use public transport?
When you feel unsafe in the evening, what do you change?
questions.help: You can choose more than one answer.

options.text: I share my location with someone
I ask someone to come with me
I use a different means of transport

questions.text: When you use public transport, what makes you feel less secure from crime or harassment? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Long waits at stops in the evening
Places with few people around (isolated or deserted areas)
People behaving aggressively or in an intimidating way
Poor maintenance (e.g. abandoned buildings, graffiti, broken infrastructure)
No surveillance or security measures (e.g. no cameras, no staff)
Incidents that happened to me or were reported in the area
Few cues to find my way without sight (e.g. no tactile paths or audio announcements)
No visual information about stops or service changes

questions.text: After dark, does poor lighting at stops or on the way to them make you change your route or the time you travel?
When you use public transport, in the last 12 months, have you been harassed because of who you are or how you look (e.g. gender, appearance, origin, age, disability)?
When you use public transport, how often do you worry about being harassed because of who you are or how you look?
When the bus, tram or train is crowded, how comfortable do you feel?
How much do the timetable and frequency on your routes meet your needs?
How stressful are unexpected delays or cancellations for you?
When the service is late or unreliable, what do you do?

options.text: I leave earlier, just in case
I change route or travel time
I don't rely on it for important trips
I use another way of travelling instead
I have no alternative: I wait, sometimes for a long time
I arrive late for work, school or appointments
It doesn't change what I do

questions.text: On hot days, are waits at stops without shade hard for you?
Do you need a seat at the stop or on board, and can you find one?

options.text: Yes, and I usually find one
Yes, but sometimes I find none
Yes, but I often find none

questions.text: Do unclear or missing signs at stops and stations make it hard to find your way?

it.#Not enough seats or shelter: Pochi posti a sedere o poco riparo

it.#Conflicts with other road users: Conflitti con altre persone in strada

it.#In the evening or after dark, do you ev: La sera o dopo il tramonto, ti capita di non sentirti al sicuro da reati o molestie quando usi i mezzi pubblici?
it.#After dark, does poor lighting at stops: Dopo il tramonto, la scarsa illuminazione alle fermate o lungo la strada per raggiungerle ti fa cambiare percorso o orario?

it.#Places with few people around (isolated: Luoghi con poca gente (zone isolate o deserte)
it.#People behaving aggressively or in an i: Persone che si comportano in modo aggressivo o intimidatorio

it.#No surveillance or security measures (e: Mancanza di sorveglianza o di misure di sicurezza (es. niente telecamere, niente personale)

it.#Few cues to find my way without sight (: Pochi riferimenti per orientarmi senza vista (es. niente percorsi tattili o annunci sonori)

it.#I have no alternative: I wait, sometime: Non ho alternative: aspetto, anche a lungo
it.#I arrive late for work, school or appoi: Arrivo in ritardo al lavoro, a scuola o agli appuntamenti

it.#Yes, but sometimes I find none: Sì, ma a volte non lo trovo
it.#Yes, but I often find none: Sì, ma spesso non lo trovo

de.#What problems do you meet at stops or w: Welche Probleme begegnen Ihnen an Haltestellen oder beim Ein- und Aussteigen?
